Bedside consultation guidance and medical record draft generation for physician review.
Local OCR and structured summary of laboratory results with pediatric age-specific reference ranges.
Teaching ward round documentation and knowledge base accumulation for complex cases.
WeChat follow-up assistance generating query lists and reply drafts for physician confirmation.
Daily task management with automated reminders at 17:00 for pending items.

timeline.title: Introduction to Local-First Pediatric AI
talking_points: Introduce the Pediatric Resident AI Assistant as a software solution with planned hardware integration.
Emphasize full local deployment on hospital GPUs (RTX 3090).
Highlight data sovereignty: 100% on-premise processing, no cloud API usage.
timeline.spoken: Welcome. Today we present the **Pediatric Resident AI Assistant**, a clinical workflow tool designed for hospital deployment. Our core principle is **data sovereignty**. All processing—speech recognition, optical character recognition, and document generation—runs entirely on local hospital GPUs. No patient data leaves the premises. This solution supports pediatric residents in managing daily tasks while maintaining strict data privacy standards.
timeline.action: Display title slide with 'Local Deployment' and 'Data Sovereignty' icons. Show diagram of on-premise GPU server.

timeline.title: Clinical Workflow Challenges
talking_points: Manual transcription of ward rounds is time-consuming.
Risk of missing chief physician instructions during multi-speaker discussions.
Laboratory result interpretation requires cross-referencing pediatric age norms.
Administrative burden of drafting admission records and follow-up messages.
timeline.spoken: Pediatric residents face significant administrative burdens. Manual transcription of ward rounds consumes valuable clinical time. In multi-speaker environments, distinguishing between the chief physician, attending doctors, and family members is critical yet difficult. Interpreting laboratory results requires constant reference to age-specific norms. Additionally, drafting admission records and managing parent follow-ups via messaging apps adds to the workload. These tasks divert attention from direct patient care.
timeline.action: Show split-screen image: left side shows a stressed doctor with paperwork, right side shows a clean digital interface.

timeline.title: Software Capabilities Overview
talking_points: Speaker separation for ward rounds (SW-1).
Draft generation for medical records with 'to be confirmed' markers (SW-2).
Local OCR for lab results with pediatric reference ranges (SW-3).
Knowledge base accumulation for teaching cases (SW-4).
Automated task reminders (SW-6).
timeline.spoken: Our software addresses these challenges through several implemented modules. First, **ward round transcription** uses speaker separation to identify the chief physician’s instructions specifically. Second, **bedside consultation** tools generate drafts for admission records, marking unclear audio as 'to be confirmed' to prevent hallucination. Third, **laboratory result OCR** structures data from screenshots, highlighting abnormal values based on pediatric age references. Fourth, **teaching rounds** are documented and added to a self-growing knowledge base. Finally, a **daily task manager** pushes reminders at 17:00 for pending items.
timeline.action: Cycle through screenshots of the software interface showing transcription with speaker labels, a draft medical record with highlighted 'to be confirmed' text, and a structured lab result table.

timeline.title: Live Demonstration of Implemented Features
talking_points: Demo SW-1: Transcription with speaker separation.
Demo SW-3: OCR of a sample lab report.
Demo SW-2: Generation of a discharge summary draft.
Clarify that hardware features are not demonstrated as they are planned.
timeline.spoken: Let us demonstrate the implemented software capabilities. [pause] Here, we process a simulated ward round recording. The system separates speakers: **Chief Physician**, **Attending**, and **Family**. Note how the chief’s instructions are extracted and archived by bed number. [pause] Next, we upload a sample laboratory report screenshot. The local OCR engine structures the data, flagging values outside the pediatric reference range for this specific age group. [pause] Finally, based on these inputs, the system generates a draft discharge summary. Please note: **AI outputs are drafts and require physician review before use.** Any unclear audio segments are marked 'to be confirmed'. [pause] Regarding the smart badge hardware: features such as automatic recording and screen OCR are currently in the planning phase. They are not available for demonstration today.
timeline.action: Screen share: Play audio clip, show real-time transcription with color-coded speakers. Upload image file, show OCR result. Generate text document. Display 'Roadmap' slide for hardware features.

timeline.title: Hypothetical Workflow Scenario
talking_points: Scenario: Morning ward round for a patient with pneumonia.
Step 1: Record round, extract chief's instruction on antibiotic adjustment.
Step 2: OCR new lab results showing improved inflammatory markers.
Step 3: Generate updated progress note draft.
Step 4: Add case details to teaching knowledge base.
timeline.spoken: Consider a hypothetical scenario: A resident manages a pediatric pneumonia case. During the morning round, the system records the discussion. It identifies the chief physician’s instruction to adjust antibiotics. Later, the resident captures a screenshot of the latest lab results. The system structures these results, noting the improvement in inflammatory markers. Using this data, it drafts an updated progress note. The resident reviews and edits the draft. Finally, the key learning points from this case are automatically added to the department’s teaching knowledge base. This workflow reduces manual entry and ensures instruction traceability.
timeline.action: Show a flowchart animation: Microphone icon -> Text Extract -> Lab Image -> Structured Data -> Document Draft -> Knowledge Base Icon.

timeline.title: Data Security and Compliance Considerations
talking_points: Reiterate 100% local processing on RTX 3090 GPUs.
Original recordings and images are deleted after processing.
No cloud API usage for patient data.
Compliance obligations (GDPR, PDPA, etc.) must be verified per market.
Include mandatory notice: AI outputs are drafts requiring physician review.
timeline.spoken: Security is foundational. All data processing occurs on local hospital hardware. **Original recordings and images are deleted immediately after processing.** No patient data is transmitted to cloud APIs. This architecture supports data localization requirements in various markets. However, specific compliance obligations such as GDPR or Indonesia’s PDPA must be verified by the hospital according to local regulations. We do not claim certification for any specific jurisdiction. Please remember: **AI outputs are drafts and require physician review before use.** The system assists but does not replace clinical judgment.
timeline.action: Display security architecture diagram showing data flow within the local server only. Show text of the mandatory notice prominently.

timeline.title: Addressing Common Questions
talking_points: Deployment: Plug-and-play on local GPU, no IT overhaul needed.
Languages: Supports English, Arabic, Indonesian, Thai, Vietnamese, Malay, Russian.
Hardware roadmap: Smart badge features are planned, not yet delivered.
Certification: No medical device certification claimed; tool for administrative assistance.
timeline.spoken: Common questions include deployment and language support. The software runs on standard local GPUs, minimizing IT infrastructure changes. It supports multiple languages including English, Arabic, and Southeast Asian languages. Regarding the smart badge: hardware features like automatic recording and screen OCR are on the roadmap and not currently available. On certification: this tool is designed for administrative assistance and documentation drafting. It is not a diagnostic device, and we do not claim FDA or CE medical device certification. Hospitals should conduct their own regulatory assessments.
timeline.action: Display list of supported languages. Show 'Roadmap' timeline graphic for hardware. Display disclaimer about non-diagnostic nature.

timeline.title: Next Steps for Hospital Partners
talking_points: Contact for technical specification review.
Schedule a local server environment assessment.
Discuss pilot program possibilities for software modules.
No pricing or delivery promises made in this presentation.
timeline.spoken: For hospitals interested in enhancing resident efficiency while maintaining data sovereignty, we invite you to review our technical specifications. We can schedule an assessment of your local server environment to ensure compatibility. Pilot programs for the implemented software modules are available for discussion. Please contact our team for further details. Note that specific pricing and delivery timelines will be provided in subsequent commercial discussions.
timeline.action: Display contact information and QR code for technical whitepaper download. Show 'Contact Us' slide.

objections.question: What is the subscription cost and hardware price?
objections.answer: Pricing details are not included in this presentation. Commercial terms, including software subscription and hardware costs, will be discussed individually based on hospital size and deployment scope.

objections.question: Does this require major changes to our IT infrastructure?
objections.answer: The solution is designed for local deployment on existing or dedicated hospital GPUs. It does not rely on cloud resources, minimizing network infrastructure changes. A technical assessment will confirm specific hardware requirements.

objections.question: Is patient data sent to any external servers?
objections.answer: No. All data processing, including speech recognition and OCR, occurs entirely on local hospital servers. No patient data is transmitted to cloud APIs. Original media files are deleted after processing.

objections.question: Is this device FDA or CE certified?
objections.answer: This product is a clinical workflow assistance tool, not a diagnostic medical device. We do not claim FDA, CE, or other medical device certifications. Hospitals are responsible for verifying local regulatory compliance.

objections.question: Does it support local languages like Thai or Arabic?
objections.answer: Yes, the system supports multiple languages including English, Arabic, Indonesian, Thai, Vietnamese, Malay, and Russian. Language models are deployed locally to ensure data privacy.

objections.question: What technical support is available during implementation?
objections.answer: We provide technical documentation and remote support for software installation and configuration. On-site support availability depends on the specific agreement and region. Detailed support terms will be part of the commercial contract.
